+import pytest
+
+from wtforms import FieldList
+from wtforms import Form
+from wtforms import StringField
+from wtforms.validators import StopValidation
+from wtforms.validators import ValidationError
+
+
+class ValidatorClass:
+    def __call__(self, form, field):
+        pass
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid", [None, 42, ValidatorClass])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sequence", [list, tuple])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stopping", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("count", [0, 2])
+def test_invalid_extras_are_rejected_before_validation(invalid, sequence, stopping, count):
+    events = []
+
+    class Child(StringField):
+        def validate(self, form, extra_validators=()):
+            events.append("child")
+            return super().validate(form, extra_validators)
+
+    def declared(form, field):
+        events.append("declared")
+        if stopping:
+            raise StopValidation("halt")
+
+    def extra(form, field):
+        events.append("extra")
+
+    class Sample(Form):
+        items = FieldList(Child(), validators=[declared], min_entries=count)
+
+    class Ordinary(Form):
+        value = StringField()
+
+    supplied = sequence([extra, invalid])
+    ordinary = Ordinary()
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as baseline:
+        ordinary.value.validate(ordinary, supplied)
+    sample = Sample()
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as actual:
+        sample.validate(extra_validators={"items": supplied})
+    assert str(actual.value) == str(baseline.value)
+    reason = (
+        "it is a class, it should be an instance"
+        if invalid is ValidatorClass
+        else "it is not callable"
+    )
+    assert str(actual.value) == f"{invalid} is not a valid validator because {reason}"
+    assert events == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sequence", [list, tuple])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("child_failure", [False, True])
+def test_valid_extras_preserve_nested_errors_and_order(sequence, child_failure):
+    events = []
+
+    def child(form, field):
+        events.append(field.name)
+        if field.data == "bad":
+            raise ValidationError("bad")
+
+    def record(label, message=None):
+        def validator(form, field):
+            events.append(label)
+            if child_failure and message:
+                raise ValidationError(message)
+        return validator
+
+    class Sample(Form):
+        rows = FieldList(
+            FieldList(StringField(validators=[child]), validators=[record("inner")]),
+            validators=[record("declared-1"), record("declared-2", "outer")],
+        )
+
+    sample = Sample(data={"rows": [["ok", "bad" if child_failure else "ok"], ["ok"]]})
+    supplied = sequence([record("extra-1"), record("extra-2", "extra")])
+    assert sample.validate(extra_validators={"rows": supplied}) is not child_failure
+    assert events == [
+        "rows-0-0",
+        "rows-0-1",
+        "inner",
+        "rows-1-0",
+        "inner",
+        "declared-1",
+        "declared-2",
+        "extra-1",
+        "extra-2",
+    ]
+    if child_failure:
+        assert sample.rows.errors == [[[], ["bad"]], [], "outer", "extra"]
+        assert sample.errors == {"rows": [[[], ["bad"]], [], "outer", "extra"]}
+    else:
+        assert sample.rows.errors == []
+        assert sample.errors == {}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sequence", [list, tuple])
+def test_valid_extras_preserve_stop_validation(sequence):
+    events = []
+
+    def child(form, field):
+        events.append("child")
+
+    def stop(form, field):
+        events.append("stop")
+        raise StopValidation("halt")
+
+    def extra(form, field):
+        events.append("extra")
+
+    class Sample(Form):
+        items = FieldList(StringField(validators=[child]), validators=[stop])
+
+    sample = Sample(data={"items": ["ok"]})
+    assert sample.validate(extra_validators={"items": sequence([extra])}) is False
+    assert events == ["child", "stop"]
+    assert sample.items.errors == ["halt"]

spec.question: Bring `FieldList` extra-validator handling into line with ordinary fields. When a supplied list or tuple contains a non-callable entry or a validator class rather than an instance, validation must raise the same diagnostic `TypeError` as ordinary `Field.validate`, before any enclosed field starts validation or any list-level validator runs. Invalid entries must still be rejected when a declared validator would otherwise raise `StopValidation`, and when the list has no entries. For valid collections, retain child-first validation, nested error aggregation, declared-before-extra ordering, and the existing stopping behavior. Return a unified diff against production repository files only; leave tests unchanged.

suggestion.description: Make FieldList reject malformed extra validators consistently with ordinary Field validation. In src/wtforms/fields/list.py, FieldList.validate currently sends extra_validators directly into Field._run_validation_chain without calling Field.check_validators from src/wtforms/fields/core.py. Require non-callable entries and validator classes to raise the same diagnostic TypeError as Field.validate, before any enclosed field's validation executes, even when an earlier declared validator would raise StopValidation. Preserve child-first execution for valid validator collections, nested error aggregation, and declared-before-extra ordering. Deliver a unified diff and acceptance tests covering invalid entries, validator classes, an earlier stopping validator, and valid list and tuple inputs.
